## Background

The Child Issues feature spans structured Beadwork fixture data, Issue Explorer state, and the rendered Tauri desktop UI. Renderer tests are necessary but cannot prove the shipped desktop application receives the hierarchy data and supports the user path end-to-end.

Triage: ready-for-agent

## What to build

Extend the real-desktop WebDriver Issue List suite and fixture Workspace to prove Child Issues work end to end: populated display in the agreed ID/status/title format and order, omission when there are none, and navigation to a child that remains selected when it is outside the active Issue List View or subsequent search results.

## Technical Approach

- Build on bsm-nd7.2 and bsm-nd7.3.
- Add deterministic parent/child fixture Issues with priorities, timestamps, statuses, and a no-children Issue needed to exercise the completed behavior.
- Use the existing per-slice WebDriver configuration and helper patterns; launch the real desktop binary rather than a renderer-only test.
- Prefer stable semantic selectors and accessibility assertions over styling-dependent selectors.

## Considerations

- Keep this task test-only: do not duplicate application behavior in the fixture helper or test implementation.
- Assert the active Issue List View/search remains unchanged through Child Issue navigation while Issue Detail updates.
- Follow the documented WebDriver upstream caveats and existing Issue List suite conventions.
- Keep test data isolated from unrelated fixture scenarios.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The real desktop suite proves a selected parent renders Child Issues after Dependencies in priority/creation order with ID, status, and title.
- [ ] The suite proves a selected Issue with no children omits the Child Issues section.
- [ ] The suite proves selecting a Child Issue changes Issue Detail without changing the active Issue List View.
- [ ] The suite proves that selected Child Issue remains in Issue Detail after view/search filtering excludes it.
- [ ] The new scenario is deterministic and runs through the documented Issue List WebDriver command.

## Test Plan

- Run the targeted Issue List WebDriver suite against the built desktop application.
- Run the affected frontend/unit suite to ensure the fixture and selectors do not regress existing coverage.

# Implementation Plan: bsm-nd7.4 — Prove Child Issues in the desktop E2E suite

## Goal

Add a test-only real-desktop acceptance scenario for the completed Child Issues flow. The scenario must launch the built Tauri application against a disposable Beadwork Workspace and prove, through the rendered application:

- a selected parent shows Child Issues immediately after Dependencies;
- Child Issues appear in priority/creation order and visibly contain ID, humanized status, then title;
- an Issue with no children has no Child Issues section;
- selecting a Child Issue updates Issue Detail without changing the active Issue List View or search query;
- the selected child remains in Issue Detail while the active view and later search results exclude it.

Keep the scenario separate from the existing populated Issue List fixture. `createIssueListWorkspace()` is shared by the success, atomic-switch, restoration, Settings, and Mermaid suites and has count-sensitive assertions. A dedicated fixture avoids changing those unrelated contracts.

## Baseline from bsm-nd7.3

This plan assumes bsm-nd7.3 has landed as described in its Implementation Plan comment. Do not reimplement that work in this bead.

The E2E may rely on these completed contracts:

- `selectedIssue` is resolved from successful `issueState.allIssues`, not from the active view's `visibleIssues` collection.
- Selection clears only when the ID disappears from `allIssues`; a Workspace transition still clears through the App-level `workspaceKey` remount.
- Each Child Issue is a semantic `<button type="button">` inside the existing `<li>` / `<ul aria-label="Child Issues">` structure.
- The Child Issue button has the accessible name `<id>: <title>. <humanized status>` and displays ID, status, and title in that visual/DOM order.
- The button uses the same `selectedIssueId` state and `handleSelect` path as Issue List rows. It does not change the active Issue List View or search query.

The bsm-nd7.3 plan does **not** promise a Child Issue `data-issue-id` attribute. The E2E must select Child Issue buttons through the semantic Child Issues list and their accessible names rather than adding or assuming a test hook.

## Existing E2E constraints

- `wdio.issue-list.conf.ts` launches `src-tauri/target/debug/beadsmith` through the embedded `@wdio/tauri-service` provider on port 46245. Reuse this config; do not add another WebDriver config or port.
- `e2e/issue-list/scripts/run-scenario.ts` owns disposable Workspaces, the isolated Workspace Catalog path, process launch, cleanup, and developer-store fingerprint checks.
- Specs select a Workspace through `TauRPC__switch_workspace`, then use the real renderer. They never seed the store directly, change process cwd, or drive the native directory picker.
- `selectIssueListView`, `expectIssueVisible`, `expectIssueNotVisible`, and `#issue-search` are the existing stable controls for view/search assertions.
- WebDriver selectors should use semantic structure and accessibility attributes. Do not select Tailwind classes or use XPath where a simple CSS/accessibility query works.
- This bead is test-only. There should be no changes to Issue Explorer behavior, Rust/TauRPC types, generated bindings, or Beadwork adapters.

## Deterministic fixture design

Add a dedicated `createChildIssuesWorkspace()` fixture with explicit IDs and fixed timestamps. Use Beadwork's supported `--id`, `--parent`, and `BW_CLOCK=<RFC3339>` test controls. Pass `BW_CLOCK` only to each intended `execFileSync` invocation; do not mutate `process.env`, which could leak fixed time into other fixture operations.

Seed five Issues:

1. A parent Issue with an explicit ID.
2. An older P1 child that is later closed.
3. A newer P1 child that is changed to `in_progress`.
4. A P3 child whose creation timestamp predates both P1 children.
5. An open root Issue with no children and a unique description search token.

Choose fixed timestamps so the expected child order is declared, not inferred from wall-clock timing:

1. older P1 / Closed;
2. newer P1 / In Progress;
3. globally older P3 / Open.

This data proves both ordering keys: creation time breaks the P1 tie, while priority keeps the older P3 child after both P1 children. Create the records in a different seed order if convenient; the oracle remains the explicit expected order above. Do not sort the expected data with a copy of the production comparator and do not humanize statuses in the test. Hard-code the expected IDs, labels (`Closed`, `In Progress`, `Open`), and titles.

Use `bw update --status in_progress` and `bw close --reason ...` at fixed clocks to establish real Beadwork statuses. Use `--parent <parent-id>` for every child even if its explicit ID is dotted; the relationship must come from structured `parent` data, not ID inference. Do not add dependency edges merely to create a hierarchy.

## Dependency graph

```mermaid
graph LR
    A[Seed dedicated fixed-clock hierarchy Workspace] --> B[Register child-issues harness scenario]
    B --> C[Add real-desktop Child Issues spec]
    B --> D[Expose targeted and umbrella commands]
    C --> E[Run focused real-desktop proof]
    D --> F[Document scenario and run full isolation suite]
    E --> F
```

## Implementation steps

### 1. Add the dedicated hierarchy fixture

Update `e2e/issue-list/fixtures/workspace.ts`.

- Add exported constants for the parent, three children, no-children Issue, fixed `created` timestamps, and the no-children Issue's unique search token.
- Extend the private `bw` invocation helper so one call can receive an optional fixed clock through a subprocess-local environment.
- Extend the existing fixture-Issue creation helper only as far as needed for this data: allow the required priority values, optional `parent`, explicit ID, description, and fixed clock. Preserve all existing callers unchanged.
- Add `createChildIssuesWorkspace(): BeadworkWorkspace` beside the other Workspace builders.
- Initialize a fresh Git/Beadwork repository through `initGitBeadworkRepo`, create the parent and children with real `bw create` commands, then establish the Closed and In Progress states through real `bw` mutations.
- Return the parent through the existing `issue` field and the disposable repository path through `path`.
- Log the explicit IDs so a failed CI run identifies the fixture topology without reading temporary files.

Do not add this data to `createIssueListWorkspace()` and do not reuse `FIXTURE_SHARED_ID`; that ID belongs to the atomic Workspace-switch collision proof.

### 2. Register a one-phase `child-issues` harness scenario

Update `e2e/issue-list/scripts/harness-inputs.ts` and `e2e/issue-list/scripts/harness-inputs.test.ts`.

- Add `"child-issues"` to `Scenario`, `isScenario`, the diagnostic enumeration, and parser tests.
- Model its exact inputs: it needs Workspace A plus the isolated store path and does not need Workspace B or the atomic-switch-only second populated Workspace.
- Extend the discriminated `ValidatedHarnessInputs` union accordingly.
- Add parser coverage showing the scenario accepts A/store without B, while the existing scenarios retain their current requirements and error reporting.

Update `e2e/issue-list/scripts/run-scenario.ts`.

- Add a one-phase `child-issues` entry to `SCENARIO_PLANS` and the command usage text.
- Provision `createChildIssuesWorkspace()` as Workspace A only for this scenario; keep every existing scenario on its current fixture.
- Provision only the Workspaces a scenario declares. Publish only the corresponding environment variables and keep all resources in the existing cleanup/fingerprint path.
- Update the scenario-layout comments and diagnostics so failures identify `child-issues` clearly.

This is harness plumbing only. The harness must not inspect fixture JSON, calculate child order, select an Issue, or write the Workspace Catalog.

### 3. Route the scenario through the existing WebDriver config

Update `wdio.issue-list.conf.ts`.

- Route `scenario === "child-issues"` to a new `e2e/issue-list/issue-list.child-issues.spec.ts` file.
- Keep the existing binary, embedded provider, port preflight, logging, and timeout settings.
- Log optional fixture paths only when present so the one-Workspace scenario does not print an `undefined` Workspace B.
- Update the file header's supported command list.

Do not create `wdio.child-issues.conf.ts`; Child Issues belong to the Issue List slice and must run through its established desktop boundary.

### 4. Add the real-desktop Child Issues spec

Create `e2e/issue-list/issue-list.child-issues.spec.ts`.

Use the same setup pattern as the existing success spec:

1. Verify startup has no Current Workspace.
2. Select the dedicated fixture through `invokeTypedWorkspaceSwitch(fixtureA)`.
3. Assert the typed response contains each explicit Issue with its expected `id`, `parent`, `priority`, `created`, and stored status. This validates the fixture and the Rust/TauRPC transport before DOM assertions.
4. Refresh once so the renderer performs its normal Current Workspace startup read.

Extend the E2E-local `LoadIssueExplorerDataResponse` shape in `e2e/issue-list/helpers/rpc.ts` with the structured Issue fields this precondition assertion reads. This is a spec-local type description, not a generated or production RPC change.

Keep selector/assertion helpers local to the new spec unless a second spec needs them. In particular:

- scope all hierarchy queries to `main[aria-label="Issue detail"]`;
- locate the list with `ul[aria-label="Child Issues"]`;
- locate a Child Issue button by its exact accessible name;
- re-query Issue Detail after navigation to avoid stale WebKit element handles;
- use `browser.execute` for one compact semantic DOM read where comparing section siblings and each button's visible child-field order is clearer than repeated WebDriver calls.

Add the following proofs.

#### 4a. Populated rendering and order

- Select All Issues, then select the parent through its existing Issue List row button.
- Wait for the parent's title and ID in Issue Detail.
- Assert the Dependencies section's next detail section is Child Issues; do not infer placement from text order across the whole page.
- Read the buttons under the named Child Issues list in DOM order and compare them with a hard-coded oracle:
  - older P1: `[id, "Closed", title]`;
  - newer P1: `[id, "In Progress", title]`;
  - older P3: `[id, "Open", title]`.
- Assert each exact accessible name follows the bsm-nd7.3 contract.
- Avoid styling assertions; the renderer/component tests already cover badge classes and focus styling.

#### 4b. Empty-section omission

- Reset to All, clear search explicitly, and select the dedicated no-children Issue.
- Wait for that Issue in Detail.
- Assert, within the detail `<main>`, that there is no level-3 Child Issues heading, no `ul[aria-label="Child Issues"]`, and no `No Child Issues` fallback copy.

#### 4c. Navigation with view/search preservation and filtered-detail persistence

- Reset to All with an empty query, select the parent again, and wait for its Child Issues list.
- Switch to Ready. The parent may disappear from the Issue List, but its detail and Child Issue buttons must remain because selection is backed by `allIssues`.
- Enter the no-children Issue's unique search token so the active Ready list has a deterministic non-empty result that excludes the closed child. Record/assert the non-empty query before navigation.
- Click the Closed Child Issue through its exact accessible name.
- Wait for the child title, ID, and Closed status in Issue Detail, then assert:
  - `section[data-active-issue-list-view-id="ready"]` is still active;
  - `#issue-search` still contains the exact pre-navigation query;
  - the closed child has no Issue List `<article>` in the active Ready/search result;
  - Issue Detail still shows the child.
- Replace the query with a deterministic no-match token and wait for `[data-empty-reason="search-filtered-empty"]`.
- Reassert the Ready view, the new query, and the same child detail. This makes the "subsequent search results" part explicit rather than relying only on a filter that existed before the click.

Use condition waits tied to visible state. Do not use fixed sleeps, inspect React state, call an extra issue-loading RPC, or reproduce `getChildIssues`/search/view logic in the test.

### 5. Add commands and documentation

Update `package.json`.

- Add `e2e:issue-list:child-issues` that invokes `run-scenario.ts child-issues`.
- Include the new scenario in `e2e:issue-list:complete` and in the changed-order sequence, so `e2e:issue-list:isolation` and `test:e2e:issue-list` exercise it in normal, reordered, and repeated runs.
- Keep `test:e2e:issue-list` as the build-plus-full-suite acceptance command.

Update `docs/agents/webdriver-e2e.md`.

- Add the targeted command to **Running it** and include `child-issues` wherever the complete Issue List scenario set is listed.
- Document the dedicated fixed-clock fixture, explicit parent links, one-Workspace harness shape, and what the spec proves.
- State that the scenario uses the same built binary, typed Workspace switch, embedded port, isolated store checks, and semantic selector conventions as the rest of the Issue List suite.
- Update the Fixtures, Scenario harness, wdio config, and Specs descriptions without changing the documented upstream caveats.

## Validation

Run from the repository root after bsm-nd7.3 is present:

```bash
pnpm test -- \
  src/issues/issue-hierarchy.test.ts \
  src/issues/issue-explorer-state.test.ts \
  src/issues/IssueExplorer.test.tsx \
  e2e/issue-list/scripts/harness-inputs.test.ts \
  e2e/issue-list/helpers/rpc.test.ts \
  e2e/issue-list/helpers/sidebar.test.ts
pnpm check
pnpm build

pnpm e2e:build
pnpm e2e:issue-list:child-issues
pnpm test:e2e:issue-list
```

The targeted scenario is the fast diagnosis path. The final umbrella command is the acceptance gate because it rebuilds the desktop application and proves scenario order/repetition does not leak the Workspace Catalog, fixture roots, or WebDriver process state.

Review the final diff and confirm it is limited to E2E fixture/harness/spec helpers, scripts, and WebDriver documentation. In particular, there should be no changes to `src/issues/IssueExplorer.tsx`, `src/issues/issue-explorer-state.ts`, `src/rpc/bindings.ts`, generated bindings, Rust RPC/adapter code, or production `bw` invocation.

## Acceptance checklist

- [ ] A dedicated disposable Workspace contains one parent, three children, and one no-children Issue with explicit IDs and fixed RFC3339 creation timestamps.
- [ ] Every child carries the parent's ID in structured `parent` data created through `bw create --parent`.
- [ ] Fixture statuses are established through real Beadwork mutations.
- [ ] Existing shared fixture data and count assertions remain unchanged.
- [ ] The typed desktop switch response proves hierarchy, priority, creation, and status fields crossed the real Rust/TauRPC boundary.
- [ ] Issue Detail places the populated Child Issues section immediately after Dependencies.
- [ ] The visible Child Issue rows match the explicit priority/date order and ID/status/title field order.
- [ ] Child Issue buttons have the expected accessible names.
- [ ] The no-children Issue renders no Child Issues heading, list, or fallback copy.
- [ ] Clicking a Child Issue changes Issue Detail while preserving a non-default Issue List View and non-empty search query.
- [ ] The selected closed child remains in Detail while absent from the Ready/search result.
- [ ] A later no-match search leaves the same child selected in Detail.
- [ ] The targeted scenario uses condition waits and the existing real-desktop config; it contains no fixed sleeps or renderer mocks.
- [ ] The targeted WebDriver command and the full Issue List isolation command pass.

## Non-goals

- Do not change Child Issue rendering, ordering, navigation, selection, or Workspace-transition behavior; bsm-nd7.1 through bsm-nd7.3 own those behaviors.
- Do not add a second Issue source, hierarchy model, RPC call, or human-readable `bw show` parser.
- Do not alter the shared success/restoration/atomic-switch/Settings/Mermaid fixture merely to host this data.
- Do not add production-only test attributes when the named list and accessible button names already provide a stable interface.
- Do not repeat the full keyboard/focus matrix in WebDriver; bsm-nd7.3's focused component tests cover keyboard activation and focus styling. This scenario proves the assembled desktop user path.

# Implementation Plan: bsm-nd7.4 — Prove Child Issues in the desktop E2E suite (revised)

## Goal

Add a test-only real-desktop acceptance scenario for the completed Child Issues flow. The scenario must launch the built Tauri application against a disposable Beadwork Workspace and prove, through the rendered application:

- a selected parent shows Child Issues immediately after Dependencies;
- Child Issues appear in priority/creation order and visibly contain ID, humanized status, then title;
- an Issue with no children has no Child Issues section;
- selecting a Child Issue updates Issue Detail without changing the active Issue List View or search query;
- the selected child remains in Issue Detail while the active view, and later search results, exclude it.

Keep the scenario separate from the existing populated Issue List fixture. `createIssueListWorkspace()` is shared by the success, atomic-switch, restoration, Settings, and Mermaid suites and has count-sensitive assertions. A dedicated fixture avoids changing those unrelated contracts.

## Baseline from bsm-nd7.3

This plan assumes bsm-nd7.3 has landed as described in its Implementation Plan comment. Do not reimplement that work in this bead.

The E2E may rely on these completed contracts:

- `selectedIssue` is resolved from successful `issueState.allIssues`, not from the active view's `visibleIssues` collection.
- Selection clears only when the ID disappears from `allIssues`; a Workspace transition still clears through the App-level `workspaceKey` remount.
- Each Child Issue is a semantic `<button type="button">` inside the existing `<li>` / `<ul aria-label="Child Issues">` structure.
- The Child Issue button has the accessible name `<id>: <title>. <humanized status>` and displays ID, status, and title in that visual/DOM order.
- The button uses the same `selectedIssueId` state and `handleSelect` path as Issue List rows. It does not change the active Issue List View or search query.

The bsm-nd7.3 plan does NOT add a Child Issue `data-issue-id` attribute (only the `IssueRow` carries one). The E2E must target Child Issue buttons by their accessible names inside the named list rather than reaching for a test hook. Add a `childIssueButtonSelector(id, title, status)` helper to `e2e/issue-list/helpers/rpc.ts` and a unit test in `rpc.test.ts`; the spec never re-encodes the selector string.

## Existing E2E constraints

- `wdio.issue-list.conf.ts` launches `src-tauri/target/debug/beadsmith` through the embedded `@wdio/tauri-service` provider on port 46245. Reuse this config; do not add another WebDriver config or port.
- `e2e/issue-list/scripts/run-scenario.ts` owns disposable Workspaces, the isolated Workspace Catalog path, process launch, cleanup, and developer-store fingerprint checks.
- Specs select a Workspace through `TauRPC__switch_workspace`, then use the real renderer. They never seed the store directly, change process cwd, or drive the native directory picker.
- `selectIssueListView`, `expectIssueVisible`, `expectIssueNotVisible`, and `#issue-search` are the existing stable controls for view/search assertions.
- WebDriver selectors should use semantic structure and accessibility attributes. Do not select Tailwind classes or use XPath where a simple CSS/accessibility query works.
- This bead is test-only. There should be no changes to Issue Explorer behavior, Rust/TauRPC types, generated bindings, or Beadwork adapters.

## Deterministic fixture design

Add a dedicated `createChildIssuesWorkspace()` fixture with explicit IDs, fixed timestamps, and one closed Issue (the parent). Pass `BW_CLOCK` only to the `execFileSync` calls that need a fixed clock; do not mutate `process.env`, which could leak fixed time into other fixture operations.

### Required Workspace data

| Role | Suggested ID | Title (visible to the user) | Status | Priority | `created` clock | `parent` |
|------|--------------|------------------------------|--------|----------|------------------|----------|
| Parent | `bsm-e2e-child-parent` | `Hierarchy parent (closed) fixture` | `open` at create, then `closed` at 2026-02-03T09:00:00Z | 2 | 2026-01-10T09:00:00Z | — |
| Child P1 / closed, older | `bsm-e2e-child-parent-1` | `Hierarchy P1 closed older child` | `open` at create, then `closed` at 2026-02-02T09:00:00Z with `--reason "e2e closed fixture"` | 1 | 2025-12-01T09:00:00Z | `bsm-e2e-child-parent` |
| Child P1 / in_progress, newer | `bsm-e2e-child-parent-2` | `Hierarchy P1 in-progress newer child` | `open` at create, then `in_progress` at 2026-02-01T09:00:00Z | 1 | 2026-01-02T09:00:00Z | `bsm-e2e-child-parent` |
| Child P3 / open, oldest | `bsm-e2e-child-parent-3` | `Hierarchy P3 open older child` | `open` | 3 | 2025-11-15T09:00:00Z | `bsm-e2e-child-parent` |
| No-children Issue | `bsm-e2e-child-lonely` | `Hierarchy no-children lonely fixture` | `open` | 2 | 2026-01-05T09:00:00Z | — |

Description of the no-children Issue: a single line containing the search token `nd7-child-lonely-needle` so a search for that token matches only this Issue. The no-children Issue's open + unblocked status puts it in `Ready`; the closed parent does not, which is what test 4c relies on.

### Expected Child Issue order (post bsm-nd7.2 comparator)

1. `bsm-e2e-child-parent-1` — `Closed` (older P1)
2. `bsm-e2e-child-parent-2` — `In Progress` (newer P1)
3. `bsm-e2e-child-parent-3` — `Open` (older P3)

This data exercises both ordering keys: `created` breaks the P1 tie, and priority keeps the older P3 child after both P1 children. The visible ID/status/title order is `id → status badge → title` and the accessible name is `<id>: <title>. <status>`.

### Notes that matter

- Use `bw create --id <id> --parent <parent-id>` for every child. The relationship must come from structured `parent` data, not from dotted-ID inference (matches the bsm-nd7.1 contract and the bsm-nd7.3 button contract).
- `bw close` requires a non-empty `--reason`. Pass a deterministic string such as `e2e closed fixture`.
- The fixture's parent is `closed` so it does not appear in `Ready` or any non-All/non-Closed view. This is the cleanest way to prove that selection survives a view change: the parent's Issue List row genuinely disappears, while Issue Detail (and its Child Issues section) persist.
- `BW_CLOCK` controls `created`, `updated_at`, and `closed_at`. Use a separate clock per `bw create` / `bw update` / `bw close` invocation.
- The Beadwork `bw list --all --json` order is the status-index order, not creation order. The Child Issues section is sorted in JS (per bsm-nd7.2), so the test asserts the order in the rendered section, not the All list. The spec never depends on the All list's order.
- Beadwork `bw ready` returns only `status === "open"` Issues; the in_progress child will not appear in `Ready`. The spec does not depend on the in_progress child surfacing in `Ready`.
- Do not reuse `FIXTURE_SHARED_ID`; that ID belongs to the atomic-switch collision proof.

## Dependency graph

```mermaid
graph LR
    A[Seed dedicated closed-parent fixture] --> B[Register child-issues harness scenario]
    B --> C[Add real-desktop Child Issues spec]
    B --> D[Expose targeted and umbrella commands]
    C --> E[Run focused real-desktop proof]
    D --> F[Document scenario and run full isolation suite]
    E --> F
```

## Implementation steps

### 1. Add the dedicated hierarchy fixture

Update `e2e/issue-list/fixtures/workspace.ts`.

- Add exported constants for the parent, three children, no-children Issue, the three create clocks, the in_progress clock, the close clocks (parent and closed child), the close reasons, and the no-children Issue's unique search token.
- Extend the private `bw` invocation helper so one call can receive an optional fixed clock through a subprocess-local environment. Do not touch `process.env`.
- Extend the existing fixture-Issue creation helper only as far as needed for this data: allow the required priority values, optional `parent`, explicit ID, description, and fixed clock. Preserve all existing callers unchanged.
- Add `createChildIssuesWorkspace(): BeadworkWorkspace` beside the other Workspace builders. Initialize a fresh Git/Beadwork repository through `initGitBeadworkRepo`, create the parent and the three children with real `bw create` commands (in any order; the order is irrelevant because `BW_CLOCK` controls `created`), then run `bw update --status in_progress` for the newer P1 child and `bw close --reason "e2e closed fixture"` for the older P1 child and for the parent at the documented clocks.
- Extend the `BeadworkWorkspace` return shape with a small typed bag that exposes the explicit IDs of the five issues, the parent's title, the closed child's title, and the no-children Issue's title. The spec reads the typed response for the structured fields and uses this bag for the visible-name parts of selectors. Keep the existing `issue` field's shape; add a new optional field rather than reusing `issue` for the parent.
- Log the explicit IDs and clocks so a failed CI run identifies the fixture topology without reading temporary files.

Do not add this data to `createIssueListWorkspace()` and do not reuse `FIXTURE_SHARED_ID`.

### 2. Add the `childIssueButtonSelector` helper and a unit test

Update `e2e/issue-list/helpers/rpc.ts` and `e2e/issue-list/helpers/rpc.test.ts`.

- Export a pure helper:
  ```ts
  export const childIssueButtonSelector = (id: string, title: string, status: string): string =>
    `ul[aria-label="Child Issues"] button[aria-label="${id}: ${title}. ${status}"]`;
  ```
- Add a unit test in `rpc.test.ts` that locks the selector shape and that the IDs and titles pass through verbatim, matching the existing `issueRowSelector` and `searchInputSelector` tests.
- Extend the E2E-local `LoadIssueExplorerDataResponse` shape with `id`, `parent`, `priority`, `created`, and `status` fields on each `allIssues` entry. The spec uses these to assert the structured Issue data crossed the real Rust/TauRPC boundary.

### 3. Register a one-phase `child-issues` harness scenario

Update `e2e/issue-list/scripts/harness-inputs.ts` and `e2e/issue-list/scripts/harness-inputs.test.ts`.

- Add `"child-issues"` to `Scenario`, `isScenario`, the diagnostic enumeration, the parser tests, and the command usage text in `run-scenario.ts`.
- Model its exact inputs: it needs `BEADSMITH_E2E_WORKSPACE_A` plus the isolated store path and does not need `BEADSMITH_E2E_WORKSPACE_B` or `BEADSMITH_E2E_WORKSPACE_B_SECOND`.
- Extend the discriminated `ValidatedHarnessInputs` union with a `child-issues` variant that requires only Workspace A and the store path, mirroring the `restoration` shape.
- Add parser coverage showing `child-issues` accepts A/store without B, while the existing scenarios retain their current requirements and error reporting.

Update `e2e/issue-list/scripts/run-scenario.ts`.

- Add a one-phase `child-issues` entry to `SCENARIO_PLANS`.
- Provision `createChildIssuesWorkspace()` as Workspace A only for this scenario; keep every existing scenario on its current fixture.
- Set `workspaceB = undefined` and `workspaceBSecond = undefined` for the new scenario, so the existing `buildPhaseEnvironment` publishes only `BEADSMITH_E2E_WORKSPACE_A` and `BEADSMITH_WORKSPACE_STORE_PATH` (the env var publication is already guarded by `if (resources.workspaceB)` / `if (resources.workspaceBSecond)`).
- Update the file-header scenario layout block to include `child-issues` so the harness's diagnostic text matches the new plan.

This is harness plumbing only. The harness must not inspect fixture JSON, calculate child order, select an Issue, or write the Workspace Catalog.

### 4. Route the scenario through the existing WebDriver config

Update `wdio.issue-list.conf.ts`.

- Route `scenario === "child-issues"` to a new `e2e/issue-list/issue-list.child-issues.spec.ts` file.
- Keep the existing binary, embedded provider, port preflight, logging, and timeout settings.
- Log optional fixture paths only when present so the one-Workspace scenario does not print `undefined` for Workspace B.
- Update the file header's supported command list.

Do not create `wdio.child-issues.conf.ts`; Child Issues belong to the Issue List slice and must run through its established desktop boundary.

### 5. Add the real-desktop Child Issues spec

Create `e2e/issue-list/issue-list.child-issues.spec.ts`.

Use the same setup pattern as the existing success spec:

1. Verify startup has no Current Workspace.
2. Select the dedicated fixture through `invokeTypedWorkspaceSwitch(fixtureA)`.
3. Assert the typed response contains each explicit Issue with its expected `id`, `parent`, `priority`, `created`, and stored status. This validates the fixture and the Rust/TauRPC transport before DOM assertions.
4. Refresh once so the renderer performs its normal Current Workspace startup read.

Add the following proofs. Each `it()` block calls `selectIssueListView("All", "all")` and clears `#issue-search` at the top so the four blocks are independent.

#### 5a. Populated rendering and field order

- Select All Issues, then select the parent through its existing Issue List row button.
- Wait for the parent's title and ID in Issue Detail.
- Read the list with `ul[aria-label="Child Issues"]` and assert the next section after Dependencies is the Child Issues section (per bsm-nd7.1 / bsm-nd7.2). Do not infer placement from text order across the whole page.
- Use a single `browser.execute` to read each Child Issue button's `id`, `statusLabel`, and `title` in DOM order, then assert the array equals the hard-coded oracle:
  - `[<older-P1 id>, "Closed", <title>]`
  - `[<newer-P1 id>, "In Progress", <title>]`
  - `[<older-P3 id>, "Open", <title>]`
- For each row, assert `getAttribute("aria-label")` equals `<id>: <title>. <status>` (the bsm-nd7.3 contract).
- Avoid styling assertions; the renderer/component tests already cover badge classes and focus styling.

#### 5b. Empty-section omission

- Reset to All, clear the search input explicitly, and select the dedicated no-children Issue.
- Wait for that Issue in Detail.
- Assert, within `main[aria-label="Issue detail"]`, that there is no level-3 Child Issues heading, no `ul[aria-label="Child Issues"]`, and no `No Child Issues` fallback copy.

#### 5c. Navigation with view/search preservation

This block has two halves that map to the bsm-nd7.4 acceptance criteria.

- Reset to All with an empty query, select the parent again, and wait for its Child Issues list.
- Switch to Ready. The closed parent's row disappears from the Issue List; the parent and its Child Issues section must still be in Issue Detail because selection is all-issues-backed.
- Set the search input to the no-children Issue's unique description token (`nd7-child-lonely-needle`) and wait until the Ready view's list shows just the no-children Issue (the closed P1 child is not in Ready because it is `status === "closed"`, so this Ready+search result is deterministic and excludes the closed child without depending on the child button click).
- Click the closed P1 Child Issue through the `childIssueButtonSelector(closedId, closedTitle, "Closed")` helper. The new detail is the child.
- Re-query `main[aria-label="Issue detail"]` after the click.
- Assert the first half of the navigation criterion:
  - `section[data-active-issue-list-view-id="ready"]` is still active;
  - `#issue-search` still contains the exact pre-navigation query (`nd7-child-lonely-needle`);
  - `expectIssueNotVisible(<closed child title>)` proves the closed child has no Issue List `<article>` in the current Ready/search result;
  - Issue Detail still shows the closed child (title, ID, and `Closed` status text).
- Replace the search query with a deterministic no-match token (`xyz-no-match-needle-7c2` is a safe choice; the spec defines the exact string) and wait for `section[data-active-issue-list-view-id="ready"] [data-empty-reason="search-filtered-empty"]` to appear.
- Assert the second half of the navigation criterion: the active view is still Ready, the search input still contains the no-match token, and the closed child is still rendered in Issue Detail.

Use condition waits tied to visible state. Do not use fixed sleeps, inspect React state, call an extra issue-loading RPC, or reproduce `getChildIssues`/search/view logic in the test.

### 6. Add commands and documentation

Update `package.json`.

- Add `e2e:issue-list:child-issues` that invokes `run-scenario.ts child-issues`.
- Include the new scenario in `e2e:issue-list:complete` and in the changed-order sequence, so `e2e:issue-list:isolation` and `test:e2e:issue-list` exercise it in normal, reordered, and repeated runs.
- Keep `test:e2e:issue-list` as the build-plus-full-suite acceptance command.

Update `docs/agents/webdriver-e2e.md`.

- Add the targeted command to **Running it** and include `child-issues` wherever the complete Issue List scenario set is listed.
- Document the dedicated fixed-clock fixture, the closed parent, the explicit parent links, the one-Workspace harness shape, and what the spec proves.
- State that the scenario uses the same built binary, typed Workspace switch, embedded port, isolated store checks, and semantic selector conventions as the rest of the Issue List suite.
- Update the Fixtures, Scenario harness, wdio config, and Specs descriptions without changing the documented upstream caveats.

## Validation

Run from the repository root after bsm-nd7.3 is present:

```bash
pnpm test -- \
  src/issues/issue-hierarchy.test.ts \
  src/issues/issue-explorer-state.test.ts \
  src/issues/IssueExplorer.test.tsx \
  e2e/issue-list/scripts/harness-inputs.test.ts \
  e2e/issue-list/helpers/rpc.test.ts \
  e2e/issue-list/helpers/sidebar.test.ts
pnpm check
pnpm build

pnpm e2e:build
pnpm e2e:issue-list:child-issues
pnpm test:e2e:issue-list
```

The targeted scenario is the fast diagnosis path. The final umbrella command is the acceptance gate because it rebuilds the desktop application and proves scenario order/repetition does not leak the Workspace Catalog, fixture roots, or WebDriver process state.

Review the final diff and confirm it is limited to E2E fixture/harness/spec helpers, scripts, and WebDriver documentation. In particular, there should be no changes to `src/issues/IssueExplorer.tsx`, `src/issues/issue-explorer-state.ts`, `src/rpc/bindings.ts`, generated bindings, Rust RPC/adapter code, or production `bw` invocation.

## Acceptance checklist

- [ ] A dedicated disposable Workspace contains one closed parent, three children, and one no-children Issue with explicit IDs and fixed RFC3339 creation timestamps.
- [ ] Every child carries the parent's ID in structured `parent` data created through `bw create --parent`.
- [ ] Fixture statuses (`closed`, `in_progress`, `open`) are established through real Beadwork mutations including a non-empty `bw close --reason`.
- [ ] Existing shared fixture data and count assertions remain unchanged.
- [ ] The typed desktop switch response proves hierarchy, priority, creation, and status fields crossed the real Rust/TauRPC boundary.
- [ ] Issue Detail places the populated Child Issues section immediately after Dependencies.
- [ ] The visible Child Issue rows match the explicit priority/date order and ID/status/title field order.
- [ ] Child Issue buttons have the expected accessible names (`<id>: <title>. <status>`).
- [ ] The no-children Issue renders no Child Issues heading, list, or fallback copy.
- [ ] Clicking a Child Issue changes Issue Detail while preserving a non-default Issue List View (Ready) and a non-empty search query.
- [ ] The selected closed child remains in Detail while absent from the Ready/search result that existed before the click.
- [ ] A later no-match search leaves the same child selected in Detail.
- [ ] The targeted scenario uses condition waits and the existing real-desktop config; it contains no fixed sleeps or renderer mocks.
- [ ] The new scenario is deterministic and runs through the documented Issue List WebDriver command.
- [ ] The targeted WebDriver command and the full Issue List isolation command pass.

## Non-goals

- Do not change Child Issue rendering, ordering, navigation, selection, or Workspace-transition behavior; bsm-nd7.1 through bsm-nd7.3 own those behaviors.
- Do not add a second Issue source, hierarchy model, RPC call, or human-readable `bw show` parser.
- Do not alter the shared success/restoration/atomic-switch/Settings/Mermaid fixture merely to host this data.
- Do not add production-only test attributes when the named list and accessible button names already provide a stable interface.
- Do not repeat the full keyboard/focus matrix in WebDriver; bsm-nd7.3's focused component tests cover keyboard activation and focus styling. This scenario proves the assembled desktop user path.
